Showroom+

Concept 8 · Direction: Recommended combination: Showroom base + Keynote compare + The Local’s fitting

This combines what worked best across the exploration. The structure is Showroom’s: light, full-width tiles that each do one job, so the three five-second messages (Motocaddy, free fitting, membership) land one screen at a time. Its weakness, slow browsing of the range, is fixed with Keynote’s ‘Which Motocaddy is right for you?’ compare row, restyled for a light page. Showroom’s single black fitting tile is replaced by The Local’s people-led fitting: the fitters’ faces, three steps and the centre’s hours and address. Identity comes from Evolution rather than Apple: brand green, the EG mark, a deep-green footer, Schibsted Grotesk for headlines (a sturdy, characterful news grotesk) and Atkinson Hyperlegible for body text, for older trolley buyers.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

Hero → M5 GPS DHC tile → compare row (trolleys) → people-led fitting → membership tile with the sum and both tiers → a two-by-two grid for Wilson, Srixon, Mizuno and approved used → secondary categories and the Trustpilot line → green footer with address and hours.

Typefaces

HeadlinesSchibsted Grotesk (variable)Google Fonts, SIL OFL. A sturdy, slightly quirky news grotesk: more character than Inter, still calm at large sizes.
Body and UIAtkinson Hyperlegible (400/700)Google Fonts, SIL OFL. Designed for low-vision readers; very clear for older trolley buyers. Its zero carries a slash for legibility, so prices and sums are set in Schibsted Grotesk instead.

Motion

Subtle: tiles fade up into view; compare columns highlight on hover; nothing on load except the hero image fading in.

Trade-offs

Does wellClearest five-second read of all eight; calm and premium; light and highly legible for older buyers; the compare row makes the trolley decision easy; fitting has real people; tiles map one-to-one onto Shopify theme sections, so staff can maintain it.
Weaker onStill fewer products per scroll than a classic shop homepage; needs the team photos to make the fitting section sing; the tile pattern will feel familiar to anyone who knows Apple’s site.
Build effortLow–medium: tile, compare and team sections; compare row needs the trolley metafields (GPS, DHC, remote, battery).
Photography neededMedium: three staff portraits and one shot of the fitting bay.
Suits bestEveryone: first-time trolley buyers, golfers booking a fitting, members; especially mobile visitors.

EG monogram: ‘EG’ in Schibsted Grotesk Bold, white on Evolution green, rounded square; inverted on the footer (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
